1.a Pre-Existing Diseases (Code Excl01): expenses related to treatment of PED and direct complications excluded
until expiry of 36 months (unless specified otherwise in Policy Schedule) of continuous coverage after date of
inception of first policy with insurer. Enhancement of SI: exclusion applies afresh to extent of increase.
Continuous coverage without break per IRDAI portability/migration norms: waiting period reduced to extent of
prior coverage. Coverage after 36 months for PED subject to declaration at application and acceptance by Insurer.

1.b Specified Disease/Procedure waiting period (Code Excl02): excluded until expiry of 24 months of
continuous coverage after date of inception of first Policy with insurer; not applicable for claims arising due
to accident. Enhancement of SI: exclusion applies afresh to extent of increase. If specified disease/procedure
falls under PED waiting period, longer of the two applies. List of specific diseases/procedures (Illnesses):
Non infective Arthritis, Pilonidal sinus, Diseases of gall bladder including cholecystitis, calculus diseases of
Urogenital system (Kidney stone, Urinary Bladder Stone), Benign tumors/cysts/nodules/polyps incl. breast lumps,
Pancreatitis, Ulcer and erosion of stomach and duodenum, Polycystic ovarian diseases, All forms of Cirrhosis,
GERD, Sinusitis/Rhinitis, Perineal/Perianal Abscesses, Skin tumors, Cataract and other disorders of lens/Retina,
Fissure/fistula in anus, Haemorrhoids, Gout and rheumatism, Tonsillitis, Osteoarthritis and osteoporosis,
Fibroids (fibromyoma), Benign Hyperplasia of Prostate. Surgical Procedures: Adenoidectomy/tonsillectomy,
Tympanoplasty/Mastoidectomy, Hernia, D&C, Nasal concha resection, Surgery for prolapsed inter vertebral disc,
Myomectomy for fibroids, Surgery of Genito urinary system (unless necessitated by Malignancy), Surgery for
varicose veins/ulcers, Surgery on prostate, Cholecystectomy, Surgery for Perianal Abscesses, Hydrocele/Rectocele,
Joint replacement surgeries, Surgery for Nasal septum deviation, Ligament/Tendon/Meniscal tear, Hysterectomy,
Fissurectomy/Haemorrhoidectomy/Fistulectomy/ENT surgeries, Endometriosis, Prolapsed Uterus, Rectal Prolapse,
Varicocele, Retinal detachment, Glaucoma, Nasal polypectomy.

1.c 30-day waiting period (Code Excl03): expenses related to treatment of any illness within 30 days
from first Policy commencement date excluded except claims arising due to accident. Does not apply if Insured
Person has continuous coverage for more than twelve months.

Master circular in force with immediate effect (except where a specific effective date is
stated). Existing non-compliant products to be modified on/before 30.09.2024. PMC must ensure waiting-period and
Moratorium-period credits accrued to policyholder are protected and carried forward.

Customer Information Sheet (CIS) must be provided with every policy
(individual and group members), format per Annexure 1, containing: type of insurance, sum insured, coverage
provided, summary of exclusions, sub-limits, deductibles, waiting period(s), Free Look Period, Policy Renewal,
Migration, Portability, Moratorium Period, Claims Procedure, Policy Servicing, Grievance Redressal contacts
(incl. Ombudsman). Acknowledgment (physical or digital) required from policyholder.

Free Look Period: 30 days from date of receipt of policy document, for policies with term of
one year or more, to review and cancel if not satisfied.

Grace Period for premium payment: 15 days (monthly instalment) / 30 days (quarterly/
half-yearly/annual instalment). If renewed within grace period, all credits (sum insured, No Claim Bonus,
specific waiting periods, PED waiting period, Moratorium period) are protected -- applies to both Indemnity and
Benefit products.

Coverage during grace period: available if premium paid in instalments during the policy
period.

Renewal: health insurance policy renewable unless product withdrawn, except established
fraud/non-disclosure/misrepresentation. Insurer shall not deny renewal on ground of prior claims. No fresh
underwriting unless sum insured increased (and then only to extent of the increase).

Migration (same insurer): policyholder can transfer credits (Sum Insured, No Claim Bonus,
specific waiting periods, PED waiting period, Moratorium period) to migrated policy.

Portability (across insurers): Acquiring and Existing insurers must jointly ensure seamless
transfer of underwriting/claim history. Existing insurer must respond to Acquiring insurer's information request
within 72 hours via IIB (https://iib.gov.in/) portal. Acquiring insurer must decide/communicate within 5 days of
receiving that information. Policyholder entitled to transfer credits (Sum Insured, NCB, specific waiting
periods, PED waiting period, Moratorium period) to Acquiring Insurer.

Moratorium Period: no policy/claim contestable on non-disclosure/misrepresentation grounds
(except established fraud) after completion of 60 months of continuous coverage. Credits from ported/migrated
policies count toward the Moratorium period calculation.

No Claim Bonus (NCB): insurer may reward no-claim policyholders via NCB, paid per
policyholder's choice at each renewal as: (a) Cumulative Bonus (Sum Insured increase, no premium increase),
and/or (b) discount on renewal premium.

Cashless authorization: insurer must strive for 100% cashless claim settlement.
PREAUTHORIZATION DECISION REQUIRED WITHIN 1 HOUR of receipt of request (systems/procedures required in place by
31 July 2024). Digital pre-authorization must also be offered.

Final discharge authorization: WITHIN 3 HOURS of receipt of discharge authorization request
from the hospital; policyholder must not be made to wait for discharge. Delay beyond 3 hours -> any additional
hospital charges to be borne by insurer from shareholders' funds. On death during treatment: insurer must
immediately process claim settlement and ensure mortal remains released from hospital immediately.

Settlement of Claims: no claim may be repudiated without approval of the PMC or its
three-member sub-group, the Claims Review Committee (CRC). Repudiation/partial disallowance must be conveyed to
claimant with full reference to specific policy terms/conditions. Insurers/TPAs must collect required documents
FROM THE HOSPITALS following claim intimation -- policyholder shall not be required to submit documents.

Claims under multiple policies: (a) Indemnity: policyholder chooses primary insurer/policy
for claim; if coverage under that policy is less than the admissible amount, the primary insurer must coordinate
with other insurers for the balance without hassle to the policyholder. (b) Benefit-based: policyholder may
claim from all insurers under all such policies on occurrence of the insured event.

Grievance Redressal: insurer must maintain a robust grievance process; response letters
must include contact details of the relevant Insurance Ombudsman for escalation.

Ombudsman Award compliance: insurer must comply within 30 days of receipt of the award, or
pay a penalty of Rs. 5,000/day to the complainant (in addition to any penal interest due under the Insurance
Ombudsman Rules 2017).

Insurers must have board-approved underwriting policy (covering offering
across all ages/medical conditions, AYUSH parity), board-approved hospital-empanelment quality policy (striving
for 100% cashless, covering all treatment situations incl. domiciliary/OPD/day-care/homecare), simple-language
proposal forms and CIS, defined claims-handling procedures and TATs, a Claims Review Committee, and prominent
website disclosure of network-hospital lists, claim procedures, and TATs for policy servicing and claim
settlement (cashless and reimbursement).

TPA remuneration must NOT depend on Incurred Claim Ratio (ICR) of
policies served; insurer must obtain customer feedback and may claw back TPA remuneration based on that feedback
(clawed-back amounts passed to the customer); TPAs paid only after satisfactory full discharge of services.
